output.summary: KEP-4188 proposes a new read-only Kubelet gRPC API, served over a local UNIX socket restricted to local admin users, that returns local Pod information (initially Pod readiness/conditions) from the Kubelet's cache so node-local workloads can avoid depending on kube-apiserver. The KEP is at stage beta with status implementable.
output.rationale:
Node-local consumers (e.g. networking components) need Pod state even when the control plane is unreachable, and polling kube-apiserver adds load and a control-plane dependency. The reviewers accepted that Pod readiness is safe to expose to same-node workloads, since the existing PodResources socket already works similarly, while sig-auth concerns about broader exposure led the authors to narrow the scope to readiness conditions. The status is implementable, and sig-node approvers signed off on the KEP.</rationale>
<parameter name="outcome_reason">null

alternatives.option: Add pod readiness endpoints to the existing PodResources API
alternatives.why_not: The authors wanted to keep the API free of kube-apiserver authorization and avoid mixing it with allocated-resource data; a reviewer asked for pros/cons. Quote: "because our goal with this API is to reduce the Control Plane dependency we didn't wanted to add this to already existing API."

alternatives.option: Use a REST API instead of gRPC
alternatives.why_not: Listed as an option in the design tables, but the discussion does not record a reason it was rejected; the KEP stayed with gRPC.

alternatives.option: Serve only data acknowledged by the control plane
alternatives.why_not: Raised by a reviewer to avoid split-brain; the response was that the API will not override control-plane decisions and exists so nodes can work when the control plane is unavailable. Quote: "the proposed API won't be used to override any decision made by the control plane."

evidence.quote: The full PodSpec may contain sensitive information, so access to this API is secured by restricting the UNIX socket to local admin users only.
We already have a Pod resources API in Kubelet that is exposed in a similar way (via socket and therefore only accessible to other workloads on the same Node).
1) Read-only 2) throttling 3) limited to small set of information initially, for example, pod condition.
I updated the doc and changed all those places to point out that we want to expose readiness information.
Basically the proposed API won't be used to override any decision made by the control plane.
